Syed Ziaul Karim, Advocate ------ For the Petitioners. 
Abdul Quayum, Advocate ------ For the Opposite Party No.1.
parties:
Ishaque Mia, (Md) & another ------ Petitioners 
Vs.
Abdul Mazid Mollah & others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned Judgment and decree dated 29.1.1991 and 4.2.1991 passed by the Subordinate Judge Barisal in Title Appeal No. 84 of 1986 allowing the appeal and reversing the Judgment and decree dated 28.5.1986 and 3.6.1986 passes by the Upazila Munsif, Upazila Moladi, District Barisal in Title Suit No. 197 of 1985 should not be set aside.

2. The facts for the disposal of the Rule is as follows: Petitioners as plaintiffs filed title suit being Title Suit No. 156 of 1977 before the court of Munsif (6th court of Barisal) for declaration that the 'Ka' schedule decree in Title Suit No. 561 of 1976 is illegal, fraudulent, inoperative, null and void without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiffs. Thereafter the case was transferred in the court of Upazila Munsif, Upazila Moladi and the same was re-numbered as Title Suit No. 197 of 1985.

3. Case of the plaintiff petitioners was that the original recorded tenant of SA Khatian No. 97 and 98 totalling 4.18 acres of land were Kali Charan Somadder, Bipin Behari Somadder, Moni Mohan Somadder, Aswani Kumer Sornaddcr, Jal Mohan, Babilal, Makkon Lal, Fani Bhusan, Bharat Chancra, Nikunja Bchari, Chitta Ranjan, Brajo Bashi and Labcnna Bela, Motillal Somadder was the sole heir of Kali Charan Somadder, Moni Mohan Somaddar, Lal Mohan, Babilal, Makkon Lal, Fani Bhusan, Bharat Chandra, Nikunja Behari and Chitta Ranjan. He as heir got 14 annas 8 Gandas share i.e. to the extent of 3.78 acres out of 4.18 acres. Braja Bashi got 1 Anna 12 Gonda share i.e. to the extent of 0040 acres. Motilal sold 2.17 acres of land and Braja Bashi sold 0.4 acres of land i.e. a total of 2.57 acres to the plaintiffs.

4. In Title Suit No 561 of 1976 which was decreed on compromise a total of 1.98 acres was obtained by defendant No.2 Abdul Majid Molla. Out of this 1.98 acres plaintiffs had purchased 1.20 acres in SA Khatian No. 177 land measuring 0.54 acres in plot No. 587 was sold by Mohan to Motilal Somadder and the plaintiffs purchased the same from him. In the said Title Suit No. 561 of 1976 0.41 acres of land was decreed in compromise in favour of said defendant No. 2 Abdul Majid Molla. Plaintiffs claim that he will get 0.18 acres of land decreed in favour of defendant No. 2. The case of the plaintiffs in the suit was that the solenama upon which the said Title Suit No. 561 of 1976 was decreed was a forged solenama and the decree was obtained without proper notice on some of the defendants. Signature on the solenama were not that of the defendants. The plaintiffs have interest in a part of the land of the sole decree and sought a declaration that the said decree was fraudulent, illegal, inoperative null and void without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiffs.

5. The Upazila Munsif on consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record decreed the suit and on appeal by the defendant the appellate Court i.e. the subordinate Judge Barisal by the impugned Judgment and decree dated 29.11.1991 and 4-2-1991 in Title Appeal No. 84 of 1986 allowed the appeal and reversed the Judgment and decree dated 28.5.1986 and 3.6.1986 passed by the Upazila Musnif, Upazilla Moladi in Title Suit No. 197 of 1985. The plaintiffs-petitioners have obtained this present Rule against the said impugned Judgment and decree in Title Appeal No. 84 of 1986.

6. It appears that the trial Court after considering the evidence on record and comparing signature of the solenama and the written statement in the suit found that the signatures were different. That the solenama was not signed by some of the defendants in Title Suit No. 561 of 1976 and was therefore found to be a fraudulent and forged document. The trial Court also found that the plaintiffs in the instant suit could not prove their title as the genealogy did not appear to be correct. The trial Court also found that the plaintiffs had failed to prove their possession-The trial Court therefore decreed the suit declaring that the decree in Title Suit No. 561 of 1976 was fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiffs but observed that the plaintiffs could proceed separately for title and possession. The appellate Court, on the other hand, observed that the trial Court having found that the plaintiffs had failed to prove their title and possession ought to have held that the suit was not maintainable under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act in the absence of prayer for consequential relief. The suit for a simple declaration was not maintainable under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act in its present form. The appellate Court also found from the evidence on record that the plaintiffs had failed to prove their title and possession. In the circumstances the appellate Court allowed the appeal and reversed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court

<u>7. Mr. Syed Ziaul Karim, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiffs petitioners has submitted that as his interest in the property had been adversely affected he was aggrieved by the decree and judgment passed in Title Suit No.561 of 1976 and thereafter has locus standi to file the present suit. Mr. Karim also submitted that as the decree under challenge was obtained by fraud and was illegal, it was not necessary for the plaintiffs to pray for consequential relief and could pray for simple declaration that the judgment and decree was not binding on him. In support of his contention he has referred to certain decisions. He has referred to the case of Hemnalini Basu vs. Md. Sabed Ali reported in 12 DLR 24. In the said case a Single Bench of the High Court in Dhaka held that a suit for a declaration that a decree is fraudulent and not binding on the plaintiff is maintainable without a prayer for consequential relief. The observation is as follows:</u>

<u>"As to the maintainability of the suit I am unable to agree with the courts below. It is a suit for a declaration that the ex parte decree obtained in Money Suit No. 14 of 1952 against the present plaintiff is fraudulent, and does not bind the plaintiff. No consequential relief is left for the plaintiff to pray for. If the decree is fraudulent, then it is void ab initio, and it loses its binding effect and it will automatically be set aside. So no consequential relief need be prayed for."</u>

<u>8. While making this observation the High Court referred to the case of Zinnatunnessa Khatun vs. Girendranath Mokharjee. In support of his view the High Court also referred to the case of Rani Mumary Devi and others vs. Siva Prosad Singh 42 CLJ 280 in which is was held: A party to suit can, under section 44 of the Evidence Act, show that a decree obtained by the opposite party against him in another suit was obtained by fraud, and it is not necessary for him to bring an independent suit for setting it aside." In another case of Bagala Sundari Debi vs. Prosannanath Mukherjee reported in 21 CWN page 375 it was held that the suit by the plaintiff to have it declared that a decree passed in a previous suit declaring that certain allegations were not valid, was not binding on her is properly instituted on a court-fee stamp of Rs. 10.00 only, because no consequential relief is needed or sought for in it.</u>

<u>9. Then in the case of Moulavi Abdul Mannan vs. Md. Rafiqul lslam and others reported in 46 DLR 493 a Single Bench of High Court Division held:</u>

<u>"When a decree adversely affects a person not a party to the same he may file a suit for declaring decree not binding on him and get the same set aside if found illegal.</u>

<u>The question involved in the Rule of that case was whether the court of appeal below was justified in holding that the plaintiffs petitioner has no locus standi to have it declared that a decree passed in a earlier Title Suit No.26 of 1977 in which he was not a party and no relief was granted against him was not binding on him, and to set aside the decree of the trial Court on such erroneous view. In that case the plaintiff petitioner was not added as a defendant but he was appointed permanent Nikah Registrar on 10-9-1981 under rule 5(4) of the Muslim Marriages and Divorces (Registration) Rules, 1994. Petitioner then filed Title Suit No. 107 of 1983 subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 163 of 1984 challenging the said decree as he was directed by the Deputy Commissioner, Bhola to take steps for setting side the decree. Though the court of appeal below observed that the petitioner was appointed permanent Nikah Registrar after temporary injunction passed in Title Suit No. 26 of 1977 was vacated and as such the decree in the said decree became infructuous but set aside the decree of the trial Court on an erroneous view that the petitioner had no locus standi and cause of action for filing the suit as no relief was sought against him in Title Suit. No. 26 of 1977 In that background High Court Division held as follows:</u>

<u>"It is true that a Nikah registrar is appointed under rule 5(1) of the said rules on purely temporary basis until a Nikah registrar is licensed by the Government on regular basis. So the said decree passed in Title Suit No. 26 of 1977 is contrary to the said rules. Hence observation of the court of the appeal below that the appointment of the plaintiff petitioner as permanent Nikah Registrar decree passed in Title Suit No. 26 of 1977 has become infructuous is correct interpretation of law. But so long a decree remained unchallenged even if it is illegal that may create complications and is binding upon the parties. It has already been noticed that the plaintiff petitioner was compelled to file the suit as he was directed by the Deputy Commissioner, Bhola to take steps against the decree passed in the Title Suit No. 26 of 1977. Undoubtedly, the said decree has been adversely affecting as a Nikah Registrar. In view of the matter, court of appeal below was not justified to set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court on the view that the petitioner was not a necessary party in the earlier suit and no relief was sought against him. When a decree adversely affects a person not a party to the same he may file a suit for declaring the same not binding on him and get the same set aside if found illegal as in the present case."</u>

10. In the first two cases referred to above reported in 12 DLR and 21 CWN the parties seeking relief against the judgment and decree obtained by fraud were parties in the suits. In a case where decree has been obtained against a party by fraud, that party may file a suit for declaration that it is not binding on him as it was obtained by fraud. In the instant case admittedly a plaintiff was not a party. In the third decision i.e. case reported in 46 DLR the court has held that when a decree adversely affects a person not a party to the same he may file a suit for declaring the decree not binding on him and get the same set aside if found illegal. In that case it appears that although a person was not a party to the earlier suit he had a right which had been adversely affected by the fraudulent decree. In that case it was proved that the plaintiff petitioner was appointed as a permanent Nikah Registrar on 10-9-81 under rule 5(4) of the said Rules. It thus transpires from the above decisions that a suit for simple declaration against a judgment and decree obtained by fraud may be asked for without praying for consequential relief if the plaintiff was a party in the earlier suit or that he was a person entitled to any legal character or to any right as to any property.

<u>11. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party said that the above cases were not applicable in the instant case as the plaintiff petitioner was not a party in Title Suit No. 561 of 1976. He did not pray for any declaration, title and possession for he was not to prove that he had title and possession. He has referred to several decisions where it has been held that a simple declaration that an earlier suit was obtained by fraud and was illegal and not binding on him was not maintainable unless he prayed for consequential relief. In the case of Almas Khatun vs. (Esahab) Mia 8 DLR 82 the defendant contested the suit mainly on the ground that the Civil Court had no jurisdiction to entertain the suit and the suit was also not maintainable by reason of the provision of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act as the plaintiff had not prayed for possession as a consequential relief which they should have done as defendant. In deciding where a suit for declaration would lie when a defendant auction purchaser obtained a similar land in occupation of the tenant it was held that a suit under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act for declaration of the plaintiffs right in respect of land which is in his possession through tenant will not lie without asking for a consequential relief where the defendant after his auction purchase had obtained symbolical possession thereof in as much as symbolical possession in such a cases effectual ultimate possession of the plaintiff. It was argued that a suit for a simple declaration would not lie if the plaintiff was not in possession of the suit land. In the case of Halimunnesa vs. Hemendra Kumar Roy Chowdhury and others 12 DLR 448 it was held.</u>

<u>"Where a plaintiffs in possession of the suit land and filed the suit for a declaration that the suit property has not been affected by the purported sale, he can maintain the suit with a prayer for mere declaration and need not ask for a consequential relief."</u>

12. This case also therefore shows that a suit for simple declaration will only lie if the plaintiff is in possession of the suit land.

<u>13. In the case of Burmah Eastern Ltd. vs. Burmah Eastern Employees Union and Ors reported in 18 DLR 709 Legal character in section 42 of the Specific Relief Act was explained by reference to certain cases. It explained that in section 42 of the Specific Relief Act the expression Legal character or status denotes a character of status confirmed in law of an individual or a number of individuals, viewed as a unit of society and not shared by the generality of the community but only by individuals, placed in the same category of character. The character itself must be conferred by law on person viewed from the standpoint of membership of the community. It is a Status or Character conferred by law. It is not a creature of contract but of law. For example, a minor cannot contract into majority nor can one, who has attained majority under law contract himself into minority it was also, observed that man's legal character" is the same thing as a man's status, A man's status or legal character is constituted by attributes which the law attaches to him in his individual and personal capacity  the distinctive mark or dress as it were with which the law clothes him apart from the attribute which may be said to belong to normal humanity in general. Then in the case of Imanuddin Rahi vs. Lilbati Das 32 DLR 75 a Division Bench of the High Court Division held:</u>

<u>"The plaintiff may ask for relief under section 42. Specific Relief Act provided that the plaintiff must at the time of the suit be entitled to any legal character or to any right to any property. Section 42 must be construed strictly. The courts are only to grant such declaration decree, namely a declaration that the decree obtained was fraudulent and void. Such a simple declaration could not be given within the provision of section 42 and, as such, the suit on the face of that section has to be dismissed."</u>

<u>In the case of Mosammat Sahera Khatun vs. Anwara Khatun and others reported in 33 DLR 442 where a Division Bench of the High Court Division held that:</u>

<u>"Before the plaintiff can be given a declaration as to her title to the property she has to prove her legal character or the right to the property since her entitlement to maintain the suit was based on ownership of property she cannot be given any relief without deciding issue on the question of her title.</u>

<u>In the instant case we have seen that both the courts below had found that the plaintiffs had failed to prove his title and possession. So according to decisions referred to above a suit for simple declaration under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act was not maintainable without a prayer for consequential relief. In the case of MA Mallik vs. NH Mallik reported in 1986 BCR (AD) 56 it was held by the Appellate Division that institution of the suit for declaration simpliciter the plaintiff for consequential relief render a suit not maintainable. The said case has been relied upon by the appellate court. Facts of the said case was that the plaintiff appellant instituted Title Suit No. 49 of 1970 for declaration simpliciter that the decree passed in Title suit No. 69 of 1961 brought by one Laksman Chandra Dhupi predecessor of the defendant in which the plaintiff was not made party was obtained by fraud and, as such, void. The trial Court decreed the suit but the lower appellate Court reversed the decision of the trial Court on the ground that the defendant in the plaintiffs suit having challenged possession of the plaintiff to file regular suit for declaration of title and confirmation of possession. In view of the matter the plaintiff's suit was dismissed under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act in 2nd Appeal before the High Court Division Judge affirmed the decision of the appellate Court and held that the suit was not maintainable for his failure to ask for consequential relief. On appeal the Appellate Division held as follows:</u>

<u>"In view of the clear proviso to section 42 of the Specific Relief Act there is no hesitation in saying that without praying for consequential relief such suit should not be maintained. The High Court Division and the appellate Court below have rightly dismissed the suit."</u>

<u>14. It appears from the above decisions that where the plaintiff is in possession of the suit property he may seek a decree for simple declaration under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. He can also seek declaration that he is not bound by a judgment and decree obtained by fraud in which he was a party. The other decisions however categorically held that where the plaintiff has failed to prove his title or possession he is not entitled to any relief under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. He may file a suit for simple declaration that he is not bound by a decree passed illegally in which he was not a party but in such A case he must show that he is entitled to any legal character or to any right as to any property under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. In the instant case both the courts below have held that the plaintiffs had failed to prove their title and possession and that in that circumstances it must be held that the plaintiffs were not entitled to a decree for a simple declaration that the sole decree in Title Suit No. 561 of 1976 was obtained fraudulently, was illegal and not binding on him.</u>

<u>15. The learned, Advocate appearing for the plaintiff petitioner has said that the court may suo motu look into the question whether a decree has been obtained by fraud. Although this is true, the suit before the court itself must be legally maintainable in order to examine the fraud. The instant suit filed by the plaintiff petitioner did not lie under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and in that view of the matter I am of the view that this court could not suo motu go into the question of a decree alleged to have been obtained by fraud when the suit before it is found not to be maintainable.</u>

16. The learned, Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party has referred to Order 2 rules 1 and 2 of the Civil Procedure Code. Rule 1 provides that every suit shall as far as practicable be framed so as to afford ground for final decision upon the subjects in dispute and to prevent further litigation concerning them. Rule 2(1) provides that every suit shall include the whole of the claim which the plaintiff is entailed to make in respect of the cause of action.

17. In the instant case the plaintiff did not pray for a declaration of title and possession and therefore the trial Court was wrong in holding that the plaintiff could proceed separately to prove his title and possession.

18. I therefore hold that the plaintiffs under the circumstances ought to have prayed for declaration of his title and possession in order to avoid multiplicity of suit and further litigation concerning them.

In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs.

End.
